source.name: Fontshare (Indian Type Foundry)
source.license: Fonts free for personal and commercial use under the ITF Free Font License (some OFL). Metadata from the public api.fontshare.com/v2/fonts endpoint.
source.note: preview.views = Fontshare page views (all time), not downloads.

items.name: Aktura
items.summary: Aktura is a medieval-style blackletter font. Its lowercase letters are a new digital/calligraphic take on traditional ‘gothic’ or textura-style forms. They look very much like the kinds of letters used on a lot of newspaper nameplates, or for certificate and diploma designs.

items.name: Alpino
items.summary: Alpino is humanist sans with a small x-height optimised for magazine design and other editorial applications. The strokes of the letters have slightly rounded corners; this rounding is more apparent in the heavier weights. Alpino’s numerals are proportional oldstyle figures.

items.name: Amulya
items.summary: Joana Correia’s Amulya is a friendly-looking typeface and an outstanding humanistic sans. Its letterforms appear both playful and nice. Several letters feature curved out-strokes: these are unusual for a sans serif design, but they definitely add personality.

items.name: Anton
items.summary: Anton is a reworking of a traditional advertising sans serif typeface. The letter forms have been digitised and then reshaped for use as a web-font, the counters have been opened up a little and the stems optimised for use as bold display font in modern web browsers.

items.name: Archivo
items.summary: Archivo is a grotesque sans serif typeface family originally designed for highlights and headlines. This family is reminiscent of late nineteenth century American typefaces. The technical and aesthetic characteristics of the font are both crafted for high performance typography.

items.name: Array
items.summary: Array is a small family of electronic display style fonts. All of the design’s letterforms are made up of dots on a grid. The capital letters in each of the fonts are 10 dots tall. Lowercase letters like the “a”, which does not have an ascender or descender, are eight dots tall.

items.name: Asap
items.summary: Asap is a contemporary sans-serif family with subtle rounded corners. Designed by Pablo Cosgaya, Asap ("as soon as possible") there are 8 styles: Regular, Italic, Medium, Medium Italic, Semibold, Semibold Italic, Bold, and Bold Italic.

items.name: Author
items.summary: Author is a family of humanist sans serif fonts. They are optimised for use in modern publications – hence the the name ‘Author.’ Its letterforms are slightly expanded, which gives the counterforms inside of them enough space to breathe, thus increasing their legibility and helps with their…

items.name: Azeret Mono
items.summary: Azeret Mono is a monospaced typeface with a mono-linear character. The story of the typeface began with a draft that was driven by an exploration of OCR fonts, past and futuristic operating systems, various interfaces and the nineties.

items.name: Bebas Neue
items.summary: Bebas Neue is a display font for headlines, captions, and titling designed by Ryoichi Tsunekawa of Dharma Type. Bebas Neue is licensed under the SIL Open Font License. You can find more details about this project here or visit http://bebasneue.com

items.name: Bespoke Sans
items.summary: Bespoke Sans is family of humanist sans serif fonts. They feature large, open counterforms, which hep maximise the typeface’s legibility in text. The family includes five weights, ranging from Light through Bold. Each weight has an upright and an italic font on offer.

items.name: Bespoke Serif
items.summary: Bespoke Serif is family of serif fonts intended for use in text sizes: this is a typeface designed for reading. The serifs at the end of the letterforms’ strokes are wedge-shaped. The letterforms themselves feature large and open counterforms, which help maximise the typeface’s legibility.

items.name: Bespoke Slab
items.summary: Bespoke Slab is family of humanist slab serif fonts. They feature large, open counterforms, which hep maximise the typeface’s legibility in text. The family includes five weights, ranging from Light through Bold. Each weight has an upright and an italic font on offer.

items.name: Bespoke Stencil
items.summary: Bespoke Sans Stencil is family of humanist sans serif fonts that look like stencil letters. Each stroke in the fonts’ letterforms breaks at the place where a writer might pause, if they were written with a broad pen. The underlying structure is similar to the Bespoke Sans fonts.

items.name: Bevellier
items.summary: Bevellier is a family of condensed and simplified sans serif fonts. The the most immediately-noticeable characteristics of the typeface are its narrow letters at its rounded-off corners. Formal reduction also plays a strong role in Bevellier’s design.

items.name: Be Vietnam Pro
items.summary: A while ago, Be Vietnam was made to compliment the essence of our beloved Tiếng Việt and was lucky enough to be adopted by many millions of users around the globe.

items.name: Bonny
items.summary: Bonny is a family of decorative serif fonts, designed for display typography. The letterforms are very condensed. They also contain a lot of stroke-contrast. Bonny’s thin strokes often terminate in flourishes; these flourishes pair well with the typeface’s serifs, which are both thin and short.

items.name: Boska
items.summary: Boska is a high-contrast ‘modern’, or Didone-style font family, with a calligraphic flourish. It is intended for typesetting headlines in editorial design settings, as well as signage, the larger texts in exhibition graphics, or any other place where you need big, elegant-looking type.

items.name: Boxing
items.summary: Boxing is an extended ‘western’ font. All of its letters are wide. They have been drawn with reverse contrast, so their horizontal elements are heavier than the vertical or diagonal strokes. This applies especially to Boxing’s serifs, which are heavy to the extreme.

items.name: Britney
items.summary: Britney is a quirky display family with very high contrast and double strokes on the stems. It lives on the border between sans serif, cursive, and script typeface.

items.name: Cabinet Grotesk
items.summary: Cabinet Grotesk is a family of contemporary fonts. In terms of design, Cabinet Grotesk is a sans; however, its letters feature of kind of stroke-contrast that set them apart from other sans serifs.

items.name: Chillax
items.summary: A new geometric sans for larger-size type in display applications, Chillax is a design bringing a 1920s modernist vibe to contemporary editorial design projects. Set headlines with it online or in print. Chillax would also be an excellent choice for embedding in a cultural or lifestyle app.

items.name: Chubbo
items.summary: Chubbo is a family of expressive slab serif fonts. It can lend a unique voice to the larger-sized texts in posters, brochures, website headlines and apps. A lot of Chubbo’s expressiveness and friendly-nature comes from the forms of its slab serifs themselves.

items.name: Clash Display
items.summary: Clash Grotesk Display is a family of sans serif fonts for use in large sizes. While the design of the family’s six styles – ranging in weight from Extralight through Bold – is generally neo-grotesk in style, one feature immediately sets them apart from other typefaces of that genre: The…

items.name: Clash Grotesk
items.summary: Clash Grotesk is a family of sans serif fonts, with a twist. While the design of the family’s six styles is generally neo-grotesk in style, one feature immediately sets it from other typefaces in that genre: Its letterforms have very small ‘apertures’.

items.name: Comico
items.summary: Comico is an informal handwriting font. Its letterforms are all-caps, and these appear as if they had been written with a slight left-lean. The design has the name Comico, of course, because its letters look very much like the style of lettering used in comic books.

items.name: Crimson Pro
items.summary: Crimson Pro a professionally produced redesign of Crimson by Jacques Le Bailly (@Fonthausen), commissioned by Google. This new Crimson is a fresh take on the original version and the result of months of painstaking work to perfect colour, glyph balance and legibility.

items.name: Dancing Script
items.summary: Dancing Script is a lively casual script where the letters bounce and change size slightly. Caps are big, and goes below the baseline. Dancing Script references popular scripts typefaces from the 50's. It relates to Murray Hill (Emil Klumpp.

items.name: Epilogue
items.summary: Epilogue is a sans serif typeface family in 18 styles (9 Uprights + 9 Italics). It also has a variable style with weight axis. The family supports a wide range of languages in the latin script scope.

items.name: Erode
items.summary: Named after a city in Tamil Nadu, Erode is a serif typeface for the Latin script. Its family includes five font weights, and all of them have clear stroke contrast. Their ascenders are long, and the letters’ counter forms are open.

items.name: Excon
items.summary: Alisa Nowak’s Excon is a versatile six-weight family of sans serif fonts; it is also a tribute to the work of the master French designer Roger Excoffon (1910–1983). Excon’s letters are top-heavy, a rarely-explored idea in type design Excoffon himself experimented with decades ago.

items.name: Expose
items.summary: Expose is a constructed sans typeface for headlines and general editorial work. It looks like it has taken letterforms drafted by engineers and crossed these with avant-garde remixes of typewriter faces. As a family, Expose includes four fonts, ranging in weight from Regular through Black.

items.name: Familjen Grotesk
items.summary: Familjen Grotesk is a sans serif typeface with a contemporary appearance intended for both text and display. Large notches, known as “ink traps”, add style to headlines and clarity to captions.

items.name: Fira Sans
items.summary: Designed to integrate with the character of the Mozilla FirefoxOS, the Fira typefaces also aim to cover the legibility needs for a large range of handsets varying in screen quality and rendering. This project is led by Carrois, a type foundry based in Berlin.

items.name: Gambarino
items.summary: Gambarino is a condensed, single-weight serif face for headlines. The font is designed by Théo Guillard. Stylistically, you could call it a post-modern interpretation of the Garalde genre.

items.name: Gambetta
items.summary: Gambetta is a family of serif fonts designed for use in text. Its ten styles are spread across five weights, ranging from Light to Bold; each weight has an upright and a companion italic font on offer.

items.name: General Sans
items.summary: General Sans is a rationalist sans serif typeface. Its letterforms feel like the France of the 1950s; they are very orderly, but also a bit spritely. The letters’ apertures are very small, making the counter-forms in typeface feel like they are being completely enclosed within their surrounding…

items.name: Hind
items.summary: Hind is an open source typeface family developed explicitly for use in User Interface design. The Hind font family includes five styles. Hind’s letterforms have a humanist-style construction, which is paired with seemingly monolinear strokes.

items.name: Hoover
items.summary: Hoover is a family of five monolinear slab serif fonts. Their most striking feature is that their letterforms do not included any curved or rounded parts at all.

items.name: JetBrains Mono
items.summary: JetBrains Mono is a typeface family designed for developers. JetBrains Mono is available as a standalone download, and is also bundled in all JetBrains IDEs. . Default version of JetBrains Mono comes with OpenType features and ligatures (which can always be toggled on & off in the settings).

items.name: Kalam
items.summary: Kalam is a handwriting-style font family designed for personal communication. Even though Kalam’s letterforms derive from handwriting, the fonts have each been optimised for text on screen. All in all, the typeface is a design that feels very personal.

items.name: Karma
items.summary: Karma was developed for use in body text on screen. The characters feature a construction style that tends toward the monolinear. Karma’s characters are economic in width, and the Latin sports a tall x-height.

items.name: Khand
items.summary: Khand is a family of compact mono-linear fonts with very open counter forms. Developed for display typography, the family is primarily intended for headline usage. Its letterforms are dynamic, and everything is designed according to a modular system.

items.name: Kihim
items.summary: Kihim in a single-weight display typeface. It is grid-based design – and a very decorative one at that. All of its letterforms are set on an extreme angle.

items.name: Kohinoor Zerone
items.summary: Kohinoor One is the world’s thinnest font ever produced. The strokes of its glyphs are just one-unit thick. As far as we’re aware, that makes Kohinoor One the thinnest retail (or open-source) font currently available in the market (indeed.

items.name: Kola
items.summary: Kola is a technoid stencil-style sans serif font. All of the stroke endings in Kola’s glyphs are rounded, and the overall effect of Paris-based type designer Jean-Baptiste Morizot’s stencilling is a bit reminiscent of the kind of lettering used on LED displays.

items.name: Literata
items.summary: Literata is designed by TypeTogether. It was commissioned for Google Play Books. Two versions of the family exist, one for print and the other for Ebooks. This is the print version of the family. Literata is licensed under the SIL Open Font License. You can find more details about this project here.

items.name: Lora
items.summary: Lora is a well-balanced contemporary serif with roots in calligraphy. It is a text typeface with moderate contrast well suited for body text. A paragraph set in Lora will make a memorable appearance because of its brushed curves in contrast with driving serifs.

items.name: Manrope
items.summary: Manrope is a modern sans-serif font family designed by Mikhail Sharanda in 2018-2021. http://manropefont.com/ Manrope is licensed under the SIL Open Font License. You can find more details about this project here.

items.name: Melodrama
items.summary: Melodrama is a family of five sans serif fonts whose letterforms feature very high contrast. Its weights range from Light to Bold. Even in Melodrama Light, the vertical strokes in letters seem about twice as thick as the horizontals.

items.name: Merriweather Sans
items.summary: Merriweather Sans is a low-contrast semi-condensed sans-serif typeface family designed to be readable at very small sizes. Merriweather Sans is traditional in feeling despite the modern shapes it has adopted for screens.It's a Unicode typeface family that supports languages that use the Latin…

items.name: Montserrat
items.summary: Julieta Ulanovsky began this project in 2010 while a post-graduate student of typeface design at the FADU, University of Buenos Aires. She launched it as a Kickstarter project in 2011, in order to complete the first public release and share it with the world through Google Fonts.

items.name: Neco
items.summary: Neco is a family of serif fonts, designed for use in headlines as well as smaller-sized texts of short and medium length. The fonts’ serifs have been designed with chunky, prominent wedge-shaped forms. The letterforms feature a diagonal axis of stress.

items.name: New Title
items.summary: New Title is a typeface family for film titles and credits sequences. Its design is narrow and utilitarian. The compressed letterforms are made up of almost monolinear strokes – only some characters have only visible contrast.

items.name: Nippo
items.summary: Nippo is a sans with an instantly-recognisable source of inspiration from the world of athletics. That’s right: this is a display typeface designed for sports jerseys!

items.name: Nunito
items.summary: Nunito is a well balanced Sans Serif with rounded terminals. Nunito has been designed mainly to be used as a display font but is useable as a text font too. Nunito has been designed to be used freely across the internet by web browsers on desktop computers, laptops and mobile devices.

items.name: Oswald
items.summary: Oswald is a reworking of the classic gothic typeface style historically represented by designs such as 'Alternate Gothic'. The characters of Oswald have been re-drawn and reformed to better fit the pixel grid of standard digital screens.

items.name: Outfit
items.summary: Outfit is the official typeface for brand automation company outfit.io. Inspired by the ligature-rich outfit wordmark, Outfit.io is delighted to release it's own type family. The Outfit typeface links the Outfit written voice to Outfit product marks; on brand by default.

items.name: Pally
items.summary: Pally is a highly-informal sans serif design. Its three weights were designed by Jean-Baptiste Morizot. Pally’s letterforms are all a bit wobbly; the angles of many letters’ strokes are atypical – just look at the capital ‘A’ – and the left and right-hand-sides of many letters are not the same…

items.name: Panchang
items.summary: Ranging in weight from Light through ExtraBold, the Panchang family has six wide sans serif fonts on offer. The typeface features letters so wide that they are almost panoramic. The family supports all European languages written with the Latin script.

items.name: Paquito
items.summary: Paquito is a small family of serif fonts for use in display sizes. Its three weights have been quite whimsically drawn by type designer Juanjo Lopez. The letterforms are condensed in width, and they all look as if they had been hand-lettered with a fine-tipped pen.

items.name: Pencerio
items.summary: Pencerio is a new take on a formal style of handwriting. Unlike a traditional Spencerian-script fonts, Pencerio’s letterforms are made from thin, monolinear strokes. These bring the formality of the past into the digital future.

items.name: Pilcrow Rounded
items.summary: Pilcrow Rounded's design is simple and utilitarian, similar to forms found on street and highway signs around the world – or in-use on cast-metal lettering for industrial products. Pilcrow Rounded include five weights: Regular through Heavy.

items.name: Plein
items.summary: Plein is a family of humanist-style sans serif fonts. The typeface’s clear and open forms are very legible and pleasant to read, too. The fonts’ letters are drawn with virtually monolinear strokes.

items.name: Plus Jakarta Sans
items.summary: Plus Jakarta Sans is a font family that takes geometric sans serif styles, designed by Gumpita Rahayu from Tokotype, the fonts were originally commissioned by 6616 Studio for Jakarta Provincial Government program's +Jakarta City of Collaboration identity in 2020.

items.name: Poppins
items.summary: Geometric sans serif typefaces have been a popular design tool ever since these actors took to the world’s stage. Poppins is one of the new comers to this long tradition. Many of the glyphs are more constructed and rationalist than is typical.

items.name: Pramukh Rounded
items.summary: Pramukh Rounded is a very condensed sans serif typeface in which all strokes end in round semicircular curves. As a family of fonts, it is particularly large; its 16 styles include a range of eight weights: ExtraLight, Light, SemiLight, Regular, SemiBold, Bold, ExtraBold, and Black.

items.name: Public Sans
items.summary: Public Sans is a strong, neutral typeface for interfaces, text, and headings. Developed by the United States Web Design System. This typeface is based on Libre Franklin. Public Sans is licensed under the SIL Open Font License. You can find more details about this project here.

items.name: Quicksand
items.summary: Quicksand is a sans serif typeface designed by Andrew Paglinawan in 2008 using geometric shapes as its core foundation. It is designed for display purposes but legible enough to use in small sizes as well. Quicksand family comes in five styles with variable support.

items.name: Quilon
items.summary: Quilon is a high-contrast sans serif family. It’s design features also transcend the centuries – elements of both 19th century English grotesques and 1990s postmodernism are present in its letterforms. The family is an optimal selection for use in display typography.

items.name: Rajdhani
items.summary: Rajdhani is an open source typeface designed for use in headlines and other display-sized text on screen. Its initial release includes five fonts. The letterforms are modularised; their squared and condensed appearance may be interpreted as being technical or even futuristic.

items.name: Ranade
items.summary: Ranade is a family of sans serif fonts designed in the neo-grotesk style. It also includes a little kick, separating it from other typefaces in that genre: its diagonal letters feature stark contrast.

items.name: Recia
items.summary: Recia is Carlos De Toro’s debut typeface with ITF. Recia is a contemporary-style serif. The family comes in 10 styles, and its five Italic fonts are ‘true-italic’ designs, which feature a cursive-structure in the letters.

items.name: Red Hat Display
items.summary: The Red Hat typeface is a superfamily of Display, Text, and Mono styles, each with a range of weights in roman and italic. The fonts were originally commissioned by Paula Scher (of Pentagram) and designed by Jeremy Mickel (of MCKL) for the new Red Hat identity.

items.name: Rosaline
items.summary: Rosaline is a casual script face, inspired by brush-lettering. Its letterforms are wide and have high stroke contrast. Being a connected script design, Rosaline’s letters all connect with one another (even the ‘@’ connects, which creates great-looking e-mail address settings).

items.name: Roundo
items.summary: Roundo is a geometric sans serif typeface, optimized for headlines and other on-screen display-sized text. Roundo’s character set is made up of top-heavy letters; this reverse contrast is particularly visible in Roundo’s lowercase letters.

items.name: Rowan
items.summary: Rowan is a family of serif fonts intended for setting long passages of text for immersive reading. It can be used in both normal text sizes, and really small sizes, too. This is due to its particularly chunky serifs and stroke-endings.

items.name: RX100
items.summary: RX100 is a monospaced sans serif font. Its letterforms are quite condensed, even for a fixed-width typeface. Because of its narrow width, the capital letters look particularly compressed, offering an interesting look in mixed-case text.

items.name: Satoshi
items.summary: Satoshi is a modernist sans serif typeface. Its design combines typically grotesk-style letterforms, with some characters that are quite geometrically-designed. In terms of its appearance, Satoshi was inspired by Modernism and Industrial-Era graphic and typographic design.

items.name: Segment
items.summary: Segment is an LCD-style display font from Frode Helland, an Oslo based designer. True to its name, all of the letterforms in the font are constructed out of segments.

items.name: Sentient
items.summary: Sentient is a serif family for texts intended for immersive reading. It is great for things you want people to sink their teeth into. The font’s glyphs are a little wide, in terms of their proportion, and this makes them look robust.

items.name: Sharpie
items.summary: Sharpie is an informal family of script fonts. It includes five different styles, ranging in weight from Light to Black. The typeface, named after a kind of marker, looks very sign-painterly – almost as if its letters had been written out quickly with a flat brush.

items.name: Sora
items.summary: SORA is a typeface family commissioned for the SORA decentralised autonomous economy as a custom solution for branding and interface design. SORAMITSU, the developer of SORA, is a boutique Japanese technology company specialising in developing blockchain technologies and well-known for creating…

items.name: Space Grotesk
items.summary: Space Grotesk is a proportional sans-serif typeface variant based on Colophon Foundry's fixed-width Space Mono family (2016). Originally designed by Florian Karsten in 2018, Space Grotesk retains the monospace's idiosyncratic details while optimising for improved readability at non-display sizes.

items.name: Spline Sans
items.summary: Spline Sans is a Grotesque purpose-built for UI interfaces, checkout processes, and paragraphs of text. Space efficiency is accomplished by condensing traditional grotesque proportions.

items.name: Stardom
items.summary: Stardom is a singe weight serif display typeface designed to be used at extreme large sizes.

items.name: Striper
items.summary: Striper is a decorative sans serif font. In almost every letter or numeral in the font whose form contains a straight line (a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal stroke), that line has been replaced with a zebra-striped pattern.

items.name: Styro
items.summary: Styro is a family of modernist-style stencil fonts. There are eight weights available, ranging in color from Thin through Black. All of the typeface’s weights are virtually monospaced, and with each weight of the family, the outside ‘strokes’ building up the letterforms increase in thickness.

items.name: Supreme
items.summary: Supreme is a large family of constructed-style sans serif fonts. These fonts feature forms that look like those that have been favored by engineers for over a century. Their letters are straight-sided, and the strokes that make them up are monolinear. The Supreme family includes 14 members.

items.name: Switzer
items.summary: Switzer is a Latin-script typeface with 18 styles; nine of those are italics. The family is a neo-grotesk design. Switzer’s appearance is classic and timeless; it might resemble earlier typefaces, but it is a new design made for our time.

items.name: Synonym
items.summary: Synonym is a family of six humanist sans serif fonts. The typeface is perfect for use in Branding and in Editorial Design projects – anywhere you need a sans that combines personality with clear, open, and instantly legible forms.

items.name: Tabular
items.summary: Tabular is a family of ten monospace sans serif fonts; there are five weights, each with a companion italic. Every glyph in Tabular family shares the same advance width, meaning that line-wrap isn’t affected by emboldening or italicising text.

items.name: Tanker
items.summary: Tanker is a single-weight, uppercase-only, condensed sans serif. The ‘caps’ saved onto the font’s lowercase keys are of a different design that those you’ll get when you press the uppercase keys. So the font has two different versions of each letter for users to choose from, really.

items.name: Technor
items.summary: Technor is a seven-weight family of constructed sans serif fonts. The sides of each letter in Technor are flat. Many of the typeface’s characters have rounded tops and bottoms; however, in the case of letters where these are traditionally flat – like in ‘E’, ‘F’, ‘I’, ‘L’, and ‘T’ – Technor keeps…

items.name: Teko
items.summary: Teko is an open source typeface created for use in headlines and other display-sized text on screen. Display families with extensive character sets are rare for any script. With Indian typefaces, however, large character sets are even less common. ITF’s designs are an exception.

items.name: Telma
items.summary: Telma is a family of informal script fonts. Their letterforms are drawn with a good degree of contrast between the thick and thick strokes. This contrast gives the whimsical structure seen in some of the characters a more formal nature.

items.name: Trench Slab
items.summary: Trench Slab is part of the Trench superfamily, which also includes Trench Round, and a special series of fonts designed to print text is very small point sizes – Trench Sans. All of the Trench fonts include large, prominent ink-traps.

items.name: Work Sans
items.summary: Work Sans is a typeface family based loosely on early Grotesques, such as those by Stephenson Blake, Miller & Richard and Bauerschen Giesserei. The Regular weight and others in the middle of the family are optimised for on-screen text usage at medium-sizes (14px-48px) and can also be used in print…

items.name: Zina
items.summary: Zina is a stately and elegant inline serif face for display use. At its heart, this is actually an early-nineteenth century Didone-style design. Its serifs are light and only slightly bracketed onto the main strokes. Several letters have prominent ball terminals.

items.name: Zodiak
items.summary: Zodiak is a family of fonts with sturdy serifs. Several of the weights in the family are optimal for setting large amounts of running texts; the extreme light and heavy fonts, on the other hand, work great together in display applications.
